Retail Store Sales Analysis & Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)¶

Project Overview:¶

This project analyzes retail sales transaction data (12,000+ records) to evaluate sales trends, product category performances, customer purchase behaviors, and channel distribution (Online vs. In-store).

Objectives:¶

  1. Clean and preprocess transaction data (handling missing values & data type conversion).
  2. Analyze sales performance across categories, payment methods, and channels.
  3. Identify seasonal patterns and yearly growth trends (2022–2025).
  4. Provide actionable retail business recommendations.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

Dropping Redundant Columns¶

Dropping 'Item' and 'Discount Applied' due to high missingness and irrelevance to macro sales aggregation.

In [14]:
column=["Item","Discount Applied"]
df.drop(column,axis=1,inplace=True)

Mathematical Imputation for Missing 'Price Per Unit'¶

Imputing missing Price Per Unit using the exact mathematical formula: Price Per Unit = Total Spent / Quantity

In [15]:
df["Price Per Unit"] = df["Price Per Unit"].fillna(
    df["Total Spent"] / df["Quantity"])

In [21]:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

data = df.groupby("Category").agg({
    "Total Spent": "sum",
    "Quantity": "sum"
}).reset_index()

fig, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))

# Bar plot → Total Spent
color=["red","darkred","firebrick","crimson","indianred","brown","maroon","salmon"]

sns.barplot(
    data=data,
    x="Category",
    y="Total Spent",hue="Category",palette="Reds",
    ax=ax1
)

ax1.set_xlabel("Category")
ax1.set_ylabel("Total Spent")


ax2 = ax1.twinx()


sns.lineplot(
    data=data,
    x="Category",y="Quantity",
    marker="d",color="Red",markerfacecolor="firebrick",markeredgecolor="yellow",
    linewidth=2,markersize=10,
    ax=ax2
)

ax2.set_ylabel("Quantity")

plt.title("Category-wise Total Spent and Quantity",color="brown")
ax1.tick_params(axis="x", labelrotation=60)
plt.show()

Key Insight - Category Performance:

  • Sales revenue and order quantity correlate linearly across all categories, indicating uniform basket sizes across departments.
  • High-performing categories contribute steadily to overall turnover without heavy reliance on a single category.
In [22]:
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
color = [ "brown", "indianred", "salmon"]
payment=df.groupby("Payment Method")["Total Spent"].sum()
plt.pie(payment, labels=payment.index,autopct="%1.1f%%",colors=color)
plt.title("Payment Method-wise Total Spent",color="red")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Key Insight - Payment Preferences:

  • Digital payments (Digital Wallets and Credit Cards) dominate customer checkouts, accounting for nearly two-thirds of total gross sales.
  • Cash remains an active channel (~33%), proving the necessity of maintaining physical cash desks alongside digital POS terminals.

Key Insight - Channel Distribution:

  • Revenue generation is evenly split between Online (~50.7%) and In-store (~49.3%) channels consistently year-over-year.
  • Retail strategy should focus on a seamless omnichannel experience (e.g., Click & Collect) rather than shifting budget heavily toward only one channel.

plt.yticks(color="brown")
plt.ylim(20000,60000)
plt.show()

Key Insight - Seasonality:

  • Monthly revenues show consistent seasonal cycles each year, with notable sales peaks in mid-year and year-end quarters.
  • Average order value (AOV) stays stable between 120 and 140 currency units across months, indicating consistent basket pricing.

Key Insight - Basket Value Distribution:

  • The transaction spend distribution is right-skewed with a long tail, where the majority of transactions fall under 200 currency units.
  • Upselling strategies (e.g., bundle discounts) can be targeted to push low-value purchases into the 200+ bracket.

plt.title("Price per unit vs Total Spent",color="Red")

Key Insight - Spend Correlation:

  • Total Spent strictly follows a linear pattern with both Quantity and Price Per Unit, confirming data consistency across transactions.
  • The distinct ray-like lines in the Price vs. Spent plot highlight fixed standard pricing tiers across catalog categories.

4. Strategic Business Recommendations¶

  1. Omnichannel Parity: Since physical stores and online channels perform equally (~50% share each), marketing spend and inventory stocking should be distributed symmetrically.
  2. Promote Digital POS: Given that Digital Wallets and Credit Cards represent the lion's share of revenue, introduce loyalty rewards tied to digital payments to increase retention.
  3. Targeted Upselling: As the majority of basket sizes fall below 200 units, introduce tiered discounts (e.g., "Spend 250 and get 15% off") to increase Average Order Value (AOV).
